$comment: A gallery item's metadata, for filling in by hand.
Copy this next to the export it describes, under the same name with a .json extension -
so '[EXP-13-R] Iron Vulture.json' beside '[EXP-13-R] Iron Vulture.nmsship'. The ingest
tool reads it on add and again on reimport, which is the same arrangement pictures use:
everything about an item lives beside the backup it came from.
Every field is optional. Only the keys present are applied, so an unwanted one can be
deleted outright rather than left empty - and a field left as "" or [] is read as an
instruction to clear it, which is how something set earlier gets removed. Deleting the
whole file changes nothing, though: it says what to set, and does not claim to be the
only thing that ever set it. Pictures are the other way round - the files beside the
export are the pictures, so removing one removes it.
Three fields are not here because the tool fills them: SchemaVersion, DateAdded, and
Source, which records the export this was read from. Images are not here either - a
picture is a file stored beside the export, named the same way this file is, with further
pictures numbered from two ('... Iron Vulture-2.jpg').
This comment is ignored, so it can stay in a filled-in copy or be deleted.

Id: The permalink slug: lowercase, hyphenated, no spaces - 'iron-vulture'.
Stable forever once published, because it is the item's address.
Leave empty to have one made from the display name. Set it by hand when two items
would otherwise slug alike, as the two ships called Rasamama S36 do.
DisplayName: What the gallery lists it under. Need not match the name in game - that can go in
AlternativeNames instead. Leave empty to use the export's file name.
AlternativeNames: Other names it is known by, shown in italics under the display name and matched by
search. The in-game name where it differs, a community nickname, the platform a
Summary: One line, shown on the card. Cut with an ellipsis if it does not fit, so put what
Example: "A hauler carrying full custom parts, textures and a palette."
Description: The full text, shown when the item is opened. Several paragraphs is fine: separate
them with a blank line, written as \n\n in JSON.
Tags: Filter tags, offered as a heading in the bar above the list. Lowercase reads best,
and a tag only earns its place if more than one item will carry it.
Author: Who contributed it, if they want the credit. Shown at the foot of the item.
GameVersion: The game version it was captured from - "7.03". Worth recording: payload shapes drift
between updates, and an old capture may not import cleanly into a much newer save.
